title: Compile a Pig Latin pipeline
description: Choose a logical dataflow and execution backend, then scale the input. The model shows where key ownership forces a shuffle and how that boundary is represented physically.
modelNote: Volumes are deterministic teaching estimates. Pig may combine, reorder, or specialize operators; use EXPLAIN on the deployed version and backend for the actual logical, physical, and execution plans.

engines.label: MapReduce
engines.detail: Pig groups physical operators into one or more MapReduce jobs.
engines.boundaryDetail: A second shuffle generally requires another job boundary and intermediate materialization.

engines.label: Apache Tez
engines.detail: Pig normally submits a DAG whose vertices are connected by data-movement edges.
engines.boundaryDetail: The shuffle remains, but vertices can share a DAG and Tez can reuse containers.

pipelines.label: Map-only cleanup
pipelines.detail: Filter bad rows and project four fields down to two before storing.

operators.label: LOAD
operators.explanation: The loader creates a relation and applies the declared field contract.

operators.label: FILTER
operators.explanation: Each tuple is tested independently, so no key repartition is required.

operators.label: FOREACH
operators.explanation: Projection removes bytes before any later distributed boundary.

operators.label: STORE
operators.explanation: A sink triggers execution of the aliases needed to produce it.

pipelines.label: Filtered group + aggregate
pipelines.detail: Filter and project events, repartition by customer, then emit one summary per key.

operators.label: LOAD
operators.explanation: The logical plan begins with a typed relation.

operators.label: FILTER
operators.explanation: Invalid and irrelevant tuples are removed before repartitioning.

operators.label: FOREACH
operators.explanation: Only the grouping key and measured field continue.

operators.label: GROUP
operators.explanation: All tuples for one customer must reach the same logical group.

operators.label: FOREACH
operators.explanation: The grouped bag is reduced to one compact result tuple.

operators.label: STORE
operators.explanation: The sink commits the final relation through the selected store function.

pipelines.label: Regular join + grouped summary
pipelines.detail: Join a large event relation with another distributed relation, then regroup the joined rows.

operators.label: LOAD
operators.explanation: The large relation begins the dataflow.

operators.label: FILTER
operators.explanation: Bad rows are removed before the join key is exchanged.

operators.label: FOREACH
operators.explanation: Projection lowers the bytes carried into the join.

operators.label: JOIN
operators.schema: flat tuple containing fields from both relations
operators.explanation: A regular equijoin repartitions both inputs by the join key.

operators.label: GROUP
operators.explanation: Grouping by a different key changes ownership again.

operators.label: FOREACH
operators.explanation: The grouped bag becomes one summary tuple per region.

operators.label: STORE
operators.explanation: The final sink triggers the required upstream work.
